screening_results.reason: This is an empirical, adult MRI VBM study comparing PTSD, trauma-exposed non-PTSD, and non-exposed controls (meets I3, I6, I7). However, the paper reports ROI-based analyses: mean GMV values were extracted from pre-defined AAL ROIs and tested (amygdala, hippocampus, ACC, insula). No whole-brain voxel-wise between-group VBM contrast results are reported in the main text, tables, figures, or supplements, so the study does not provide the required whole-brain voxel-wise PTSD vs control GM volume comparisons (I4 not met). Therefore Exclusion criterion E4 (ROI-only reporting with no qualifying whole-brain results) applies. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (SPM12/DARTEL) that includes a PTSD group (n=91) and healthy controls. The paper reports whole-brain voxel-wise between-group contrasts (PTSD vs HC as part of diagnosis-specific comparisons and inclusive masking) with voxel-wise results and FWE-corrected coordinates (putamen increases reported with x/y/z and p-values). PTSD diagnosis was established with PCL and CAPS. Participants are adult earthquake survivors (no indication of a pediatric sample), and controls are healthy individuals—both acceptable per criteria. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and provides the qualifying whole-brain results in text/figures. Therefore the study satisfies I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) that reports whole-brain voxel-wise between-group contrasts of PTSD patients versus controls (PTSD vs HC and PTSD vs TC) with significant GM volume differences reported in tables/figures and described in the text. Control groups include both healthy and trauma-exposed controls. Participants are adults (18–50 years). The full text includes Introduction, Methods (VBM, MRI protocol, participants), Results (whole-brain contrasts and correlations), and Discussion. Therefore it meets all listed inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) and violates none of the exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This study is excluded because it does not report any whole-brain voxel-wise between-group contrast of PTSD patients versus controls. Exclusion criteria met: E9 (longitudinal study without a qualifying between-group PTSD vs control contrast) and E10 (reports only within-group/associative results rather than a PTSD vs control comparison). Inclusion criteria met: I7 (adult human sample). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (does not assess GM volume differences between PTSD patients and controls), I4 (does not report a whole-brain voxel-wise PTSD vs control GM contrast), I6 (no control population comparison reported). Although the paper includes a VBM (whole-brain) analysis, this analysis tests within-group associations (change in gray matter volume correlated with change in posttraumatic anhedonia) rather than a PTSD vs control between-group contrast required by the meta-analysis. Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry to compare grey matter volume between adult PTSD patients (n=21) and trauma-exposed controls (n=17). The paper reports whole-brain voxel-wise between-group contrasts (SPM2 VBM) with family-wise error correction and provides stereotactic coordinates for hippocampal and anterior cingulate findings. Control group is trauma-exposed and both groups are adults. The full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not pediatric, not non-voxel methods, not non-empirical, reports significant between-group results). Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical English-language MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) reporting whole-brain voxel-wise between-group contrasts of GM volume between PTSD and control groups; controls were non-traumatized healthy youth. However, the sample is pediatric (ages 8–18), so the study does not meet the adult-sample inclusion criterion (I7) and therefore meets exclusion criterion E6 (paediatric/adolescent study). Inclusion criteria met: I3, I4, I5, I6. Inclusion criterion not met: I7. Exclusion criterion applied: E6. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical adult VBM study of PTSD but it does not include any between-group contrast comparing PTSD patients to control participants. Instead, analyses compare PTSD subgroups (dissociative subtype vs non-dissociative PTSD) and report correlations across PTSD participants. Therefore it fails the requirement for a PTSD vs control whole-brain voxel-wise GM contrast. Exclusion IDs met: E10 (only within-group/subgroup results without a qualifying PTSD vs control contrast). Inclusion IDs met: I7 (adult human sample). Inclusion IDs not met: I3 (MRI GM volume differences between PTSD patients and controls), I4 (whole-brain voxel-wise PTSD vs control contrast). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical, English-language VBM structural MRI study in adults that reports whole-brain voxel-wise between-group analyses comparing PTSD patients and trauma-exposed healthy controls. The methods explicitly describe whole-brain VBM-DARTEL analyses and group contrasts; results report significant GM volume reductions in clinical groups versus controls and report voxel-wise interaction and covariate analyses (coordinates/tables/figures referenced). Control group is trauma-exposed, and participants are adults (mean ages ~33–36). Full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6 and I7; no exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical structural MRI VBM study comparing GM volume in PTSD (CSA-related) adolescents vs healthy controls. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (empirical English MRI study reporting GM volume differences), I4 (reports a whole-brain voxel-wise between-group GLM/contrast, albeit null), I5 (results reported in text/figures), and I6 (healthy control group). Inclusion criterion I7 (adult sample: both groups ≥18 years) is NOT met — the sample is explicitly adolescents (age 12–21, described as paediatric/adolescent). Exclusion criterion E6 (paediatric/adolescent studies) therefore applies. Because the review restricts to adult samples, this study must be excluded. Full text appears complete.

This is a longitudinal treatment study comparing PTSD patients who received psychotherapy to a waiting-list PTSD control; no healthy or trauma-exposed non-PTSD control group is included and no whole-brain voxel-wise between-group contrast of PTSD patients vs controls is reported. The paper reports ROI analyses (hippocampus and amygdala) and group-by-time effects within PTSD patients, but does not provide the qualifying whole-brain PTSD vs control contrasts required for the meta-analysis. Inclusion criteria met: I7 (adult human sample). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no PTSD vs control GM volume comparison), I4 (no whole-brain voxel-wise PTSD vs control contrast), I6 (control group are PTSD waiting-list, not healthy/trauma-exposed non-PTSD). Exclusion criteria met: E4 (only ROI analyses/no qualifying whole-brain results), E9 (treatment/longitudinal study without qualifying PTSD vs control contrast), and E10 (no between-group PTSD vs controls contrast reported). Full text appears complete. Therefore exclude from the PTSD morphometry meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, English-language MRI study that performed voxel-based morphometry (VBM) using whole-brain, voxel-wise analyses (DARTEL in SPM8) comparing gray matter volumes between adult PTSD patients (combat veterans) and trauma-exposed controls. Between-group contrasts are reported (VOXEL-wise results, Table 3) including coordinates and thresholding details (uncorrected P<0.001 reported, with FWE results noted). Controls are trauma-exposed veterans without PTSD and all participants are adults. Although group differences did not survive strict FWE correction, the paper presents whole-brain voxel-wise between-group GM comparisons and coordinates, satisfying the meta-analysis inclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria were met.

Exclusion: E10. This study is excluded because it does not report a whole-brain voxel-wise between-group GMV contrast of PTSD patients versus controls. While the paper includes VBM whole-brain regression analyses relating self-blame to GMV and reports peak MNI coordinates for a lingual cluster, the PTSD vs non-PTSD/NEC comparison was performed only on the extracted cluster (ANOVA on ROI values) rather than as a whole-brain voxel-wise between-group contrast. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (empirical English MRI study with PTSD subgroup and reported GMV differences at the extracted-cluster level), I5 (coordinates/statistics for reported cluster are provided), I6 (appropriate control populations), I7 (adult human sample). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no whole-brain voxel-wise between-group PTSD vs control GMV contrast). Full text appears complete. Therefore exclude under E10.

This study is a VBM within-group analysis of Functional Neurological Disorder (FND) patients examining correlations between PTSD symptom severity, childhood abuse and gray matter volumes. It does not include a between-group voxel-wise comparison of PTSD patients versus controls. Therefore it fails to meet key inclusion criteria I3 (MRI study assessing GM volume differences between PTSD patients and controls) and I4 (reports at least one whole-brain voxel-wise between-group PTSD vs control contrast). It reports only within-group correlations in an FND sample and no PTSD patient group comparison; thus exclusion criterion E10 (only within-group results without a qualifying between-group PTSD vs control contrast) is applicable. Inclusion criterion I7 (adult human sample) is met. Conclusion: EXCLUDED because no PTSD vs control whole-brain VBM comparison (I3 and I4 not met); exclusion E10 applied.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to compare gray-matter concentrations between adult PTSD patients (child abuse–related complex PTSD, n=31) and matched healthy controls (n=28). The paper reports whole-brain voxel-wise between-group contrasts with significant GM reductions (hippocampus, ACC, OFC, DLPFC, SMA), provides peak coordinates and figures, and includes regression analyses linking volumes to clinical measures. Controls are healthy nonexposed individuals and all participants are adults. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, pediatric sample, non-voxel methods, non-empirical, null-only, or treatment-only designs) are met. Therefore the study satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 and should be included in the meta-analysis of VBM morphometry studies of PTSD-related gray-matter alterations.

This is an empirical, English-language MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to compare grey matter volume between adults with current PTSD (n=15) and trauma-exposed non-PTSD controls (n=17). The paper reports whole-brain voxel-wise between-group contrasts (NS > S and S > NS) and voxel-wise regressions with dissociation scores, with results presented in tables/figures and coordinates (Table 3, Figs. 1–2). Controls are trauma-exposed non-PTSD individuals. Participants are adult employees (train drivers, ticket collectors, service staff); the full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not non-empirical, not pediatric, uses voxel-based VBM whole-brain analyses, presents between-group PTSD vs controls contrasts with significant results). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study reports only within-sample, symptom-severity (continuous CAPS) voxelwise regressions relating PTSD severity to gray matter volume in a single group of combat-exposed veterans (N=32, 15 with PTSD). It does not report any whole-brain voxel-wise between-group contrast comparing a PTSD patient group versus a control group (trauma-exposed or healthy). Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E10 (only within-group results without a qualifying PTSD vs control between-group contrast). Inclusion criteria met: I7 (adult sample). Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no PTSD vs control GM volume comparison), I4 (no whole-brain voxel-wise between-group PTSD vs control contrast), I6 (no control population). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This study reports only within-group voxel-based morphometry analyses relating grey matter volume to symptom severity within a PTSD sample and does not include any whole-brain voxel-wise between-group contrasts of PTSD patients versus controls. (a) Exclusion criteria met: E10 (only within-group results without qualifying between-group PTSD vs control contrast). (b) Inclusion criteria met: I7 (adult human sample). (c) Inclusion criteria not met: I3 (no MRI GM volume differences reported between PTSD and controls), I4 (no whole-brain voxel-wise between-group PTSD vs control contrast), I6 (no control group reported). Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion). Therefore the study must be excluded from a meta-analysis requiring between-group whole-brain GM contrasts.

This is a longitudinal multimodal MRI study of pediatric PTSD with participants aged 8–18 described explicitly as youths/adolescents. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (empirical MRI study assessing GM volume differences between PTSD and controls), I4 (reports whole-brain voxel-wise VBM between-group contrasts), I5 (results reported in text/tables/figures), and I6 (controls were nontraumatized typically developing youths). Inclusion criterion I7 (adult sample) is not met because the sample is pediatric/adolescent. Exclusion criteria met: E6 (paediatric, child or adolescent study). The full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore excluded solely due to sample age not matching adult-only requirement for the meta-analysis.

This is a pediatric sample (PTSD subjects ages 4–17), so it does not meet the adult-sample requirement (I7) and thus meets exclusion criterion E6. The study uses manual/segmented ROI hippocampal volumetry (non–voxel-based methods) and does not report any whole-brain voxel-wise grey-matter contrasts (no VBM/whole-brain coordinate-based results), so it fails I4 and meets exclusion criteria E4 and E7. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (empirical MRI study assessing GM volume differences via hippocampal segmentation) and I6 (control population: healthy non-maltreated controls). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no whole-brain voxel-wise GM contrast) and I7 (sample is pediatric, not adult). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study must be excluded from this adult, whole-brain voxel-based GM meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) reporting whole-brain, voxel-wise between-group contrasts (ANOVA and post-hoc) comparing adult PTSD patients (n=27) to trauma-exposed controls (n=33) and healthy controls (n=30). Significant whole-brain GM volume reductions (bilateral hippocampus and left lingual gyrus) are reported with voxel and cluster thresholds and correlations with symptom scores; results are presented in figures and described in text. The sample consists of adults exposed to a typhoon; controls include both trauma-exposed and non-exposed adults. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, pediatric sample, non-voxel methods, non-empirical, null-only results, or absence of PTSD vs control contrasts) are met.

This is an empirical, English-language VBM MRI study of adult PTSD patients vs controls assessing gray-matter volume (I3 satisfied). It reports voxel-wise results (figures and MNI coordinates) and uses acceptable reporting formats (I5 satisfied), includes adult subjects (I7) and healthy non-traumatized controls (I6). However, the voxel-wise GMV comparisons were performed within a combined hippocampus/amygdala mask rather than as a whole-brain voxel-wise between-group contrast, so it does not meet the review’s whole-brain requirement (I4 not met) and therefore falls under exclusion criterion E4 (ROI/masked analyses only). Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I3, I5, I6, I7. Inclusion criteria not met: I4. Exclusion criteria met: E4.

This is a pediatric study (participants aged 6–16), so it fails the adult-sample inclusion criterion (I7) and meets exclusion E6. The morphometry methods are region-based parcellation/volumetry and DTI tractography rather than whole-brain voxel-wise (VBM) GM contrasts required by I4; thus it violates the morphometry-methods inclusion and meets exclusion E7. The study is empirical MRI research with PTSD and trauma/non-trauma controls (I3 and I6 are satisfied), but it does not provide the required voxel-wise whole-brain GM between-group contrasts in adults. Therefore it must be excluded.

This is an empirical, English-language MRI study of adult breast cancer survivors (ages 18–55) with PTSD compared to trauma-exposed and healthy controls. It uses voxel-based morphometry (VBM) and reports whole-brain voxel-wise between-group contrasts (PTSD vs non-PTSD and vs healthy controls), with coordinates and statistical maps reported. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and presents longitudinal data but also cross-sectional between-group contrasts at baseline. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not pediatric, not non-empirical, uses voxel-based whole-brain morphometry). Therefore it meets all required inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to compare gray-matter volume between PTSD patients and controls. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. The analysis reports whole-brain voxel-wise between-group contrasts (victims with PTSD, n=9, vs trauma-exposed victims without PTSD, n=16) and identifies a significant left anterior cingulate cortex gray-matter reduction; correlational analysis with CAPS severity is also reported. Controls are trauma-exposed non-PTSD individuals (eligible per criteria). Subjects are adults (Tokyo subway sarin victims assessed 5–6 years post-incident). The paper therefore meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not non-voxel methods only, not pediatric, not non-empirical, not solely null results). Full text appears complete. Inclusion is appropriate for a meta-analysis of morphometry studies of structural alterations associated with PTSD.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) in adult (mean age 29.6) combat veterans. It reports whole-brain, voxel-wise regression analyses of CAPS (PTSS) and a voxel-wise between-group contrast (PTSD vs non-PTSD) comparing gray matter volume, with significant regional results reported in tables/figures (sgACC, insula, caudate, etc.). Controls are trauma-exposed (non-PTSD veterans). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Thus all required inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical English-language MRI study of adult PTSD vs controls (meets I3, I6, I7). However, it does not report a whole-brain voxel-wise GM (VBM) between-group contrast. Analyses are surface-based (FreeSurfer parcellated cortical volumes and vertex-wise cortical thickness) and parcelwise comparisons; no voxel-based whole-brain GM VBM results are provided. Therefore it meets exclusion criterion E7 (non-voxel-based morphometry only). Inclusion I4 (whole-brain voxel-wise GM contrast) is not met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical human MRI study using optimized voxel-based morphometry (VBM) with whole-brain, voxel-wise between-group contrasts comparing grey matter volume in adult PTSD patients (drug‑naïve) versus healthy controls. The paper reports MNI coordinates, cluster statistics and between-group comparisons at baseline and longitudinal group×time interactions (pre- vs post-EMDR vs controls) in the main text and tables, fulfilling whole-brain voxel-wise reporting. Controls are healthy adults and patient and control groups are adults (age range 18–65). The full text contains Introduction, Methods (MRI acquisition and VBM procedures), Results (including coordinates and F-values), and Discussion, and reports findings in English sections (methods/results), satisfying the English-language reporting requirement. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not non-empirical, not pediatric, used voxel-based methods, included between-group contrasts).

Although this is an empirical English VBM MRI study with adult PTSD patients and healthy controls (meets I3, I6, I7), the paper does not provide a qualifying whole-brain voxel-wise between-group contrast of PTSD patients vs controls with reported coordinates or significant results (I4 not met). The PTSD vs control comparisons are either not reported or yielded null results; thus the study effectively provides no qualifying PTSD-vs-control whole-brain GM differences and meets exclusion E11 (reports only null/no qualifying PTSD vs control differences). Full text appears complete.

This study is excluded because it does not report a whole-brain voxel-wise (VBM) between-group contrast of GM volume for PTSD patients vs controls. Exclusion criteria met: E4 (the study reports only region-based morphometry/ROI analyses with no qualifying whole-brain VBM results) and E7 (morphometry was performed using non-voxel-based RBM/region-based measures with no voxel-wise VBM contrast). Inclusion criteria satisfied: I3 (empirical English-language MRI study assessing gray matter volume differences between PTSD patients and controls), I6 (control groups include healthy and trauma-exposed individuals), I7 (adult sample). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no whole-brain voxel-wise GM contrast reported). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion provided). Therefore the paper must be excluded from a meta-analysis that requires whole-brain VBM contrasts.

This study is an empirical English-language MRI study of adult PTSD patients vs controls using both manual volumetry and voxel-based morphometry (VBM) with voxel-wise, whole-brain two-sample t-tests (SPM2). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (MRI GM volume study), I4 (whole-brain voxel-wise between-group VBM contrast reported), I5 (results reported in main text), I6 (healthy control group), I7 (adult sample). However, the paper reports only null between-group results (no significant GM differences by VBM or manual volumetry). Per exclusion criterion E11 (studies that report only null results), this study must be excluded from the meta-analysis. Inclusion criteria not met: none (all relevant inclusion criteria I3,I4,I5,I6,I7 are satisfied). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using optimized voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to compare gray matter density between 21 adult PTSD patients and 22 trauma-exposed non-PTSD controls. The paper reports whole-brain, voxel-wise between-group contrasts (NS > S and R > NR) with cluster-level correction and provides Talairach coordinates and tables/figures of results. Controls are trauma-exposed non-PTSD adults. An adult working cohort is described. Although the paper includes an EMDR treatment subset, the main between-group PTSD vs trauma-exposed control VBM contrasts satisfy the meta-analysis requirements.

This is an empirical English-language MRI study reporting gray-matter volumetric comparisons between PTSD and control groups (meets I3) using healthy nonmaltreated controls (meets I6). However, it is a pediatric sample of children and adolescents (explicitly described as maltreated children and adolescents with PTSD), violating adult-sample requirement (E6). The morphometry used manual, ROI-based volumetric tracing of the superior temporal gyrus rather than whole-brain voxel-wise (VBM) analyses, violating the requirement for whole-brain voxel-wise GM contrasts (I4) and matching exclusion for ROI-only/non-voxel-based methods (E4 and E7). Therefore it does not provide the necessary whole-brain voxel-wise GM between-group contrasts among adults required for inclusion.

This is an empirical English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (SPM5 with DARTEL) comparing gray matter volume between adult PTSD patients and trauma-exposed controls. The paper reports whole-brain, voxel-wise between-group contrasts (FDR-corrected p<0.05) showing significant GM reductions (ventral premotor cortex and pregenual anterior cingulate), with results described in text and figures; ROI analyses for hippocampus/amygdala are also reported but whole-brain results are present. Both groups are trauma-exposed adults (recruited from outpatient clinic and university employees), and PTSD diagnosis was established with SCID. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria for the morphometry PTSD meta-analysis are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study is an empirical MRI morphometry study in English that reports gray matter volume differences between PTSD patients and controls using both ROI and voxel-based morphometry (VBM). The abstract and results describe significant voxel clusters for group affiliation in the right hippocampus from a multiple regression VBM model (a whole-brain, voxel-wise between-group contrast), and ROI analyses reported decreased hippocampal volumes. Controls were healthy individuals. Participants are described as patients and controls consistent with adult clinical samples; absence of explicit ages in the available content does not preclude inclusion by the review rules. However, the provided full-text content appears incomplete (primarily abstract, metadata, and references rather than full methods/results/discussion), so I flagged fulltext_incomplete=true and assigned moderate confidence.

This is an empirical, English-language VBM MRI study of adult combat veterans with PTSD vs trauma-exposed controls (meets I3, I6, I7). However, the analysis is an ROI-based VBM approach: authors extracted eigenvariates from a priori olfactory ROIs and report ANCOVAs on those ROIs rather than presenting a whole-brain voxel-wise between-group contrast. The paper does not report qualifying whole-brain voxel-wise GM volume contrasts of PTSD patients vs controls, so it fails I4 and meets exclusion criterion E4 (ROI-only results with no whole-brain results). Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical adult MRI study reporting grey-matter volume differences between PTSD patients and controls (meets I3) and reports VBM cluster coordinates/figures (meets I5). Controls include trauma-exposed and nontraumatized groups (meets I6), and all participants are adults (meets I7). However, the voxel-based morphometry analyses were performed with ROI masking based on FreeSurfer parcellation rather than as an unrestricted whole-brain voxel-wise between-group contrast. The paper does not report an unmasked whole-brain voxel-wise GM contrast of PTSD vs controls, so it fails inclusion criterion I4. Because only ROI-masked VBM (i.e., ROI-only voxel-wise results) are reported with no qualifying whole-brain voxel-wise results, exclusion criterion E4 applies. Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical English MRI study of adult PTSD patients and healthy controls that reports gray-matter and subcortical volumes using SIENAX and FSL FIRST (I3, I6, I7 met). However, the study does not report any whole-brain voxel-wise (VBM) between-group contrasts or coordinate-based results. Morphometry was performed using non–voxel-based methods (global GM/TBV measures and subcortical segmentation/ROI volumes) and no voxel-wise statistical maps or coordinates are provided. Therefore it fails the required whole-brain voxel-wise evidence criterion (I4 not met) and meets exclusion criteria E4 (only ROI/non–whole-brain results) and E7 (non-voxel-based morphometry only). Full text appears complete. Exclusion summary: (a) exclusion IDs met: E4, E7; (b) inclusion IDs met: I3, I6, I7; (c) inclusion IDs not met: I4. Consequently the study should be excluded from the voxel-wise GM meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, English-language MRI study comparing gray-matter volumes between adult PTSD patients (drug-naïve, mean age ~38, trauma in adulthood) and matched healthy controls, using both SIENAX and a VBM-style (voxel-wise) whole-brain analysis. The paper reports voxel-wise between-group contrasts (FSL-VBM 'randomize' permutations, cluster corrected results) with tables/figures of significant clusters (frontal and occipital decreases), satisfying whole-brain VBM reporting. Control group are healthy individuals. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text is complete. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, pediatric sample, non-voxel-only methods, non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets all listed inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6, I7) and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to compare grey-matter volume between adult PTSD patients and controls (survivors of the same trauma without PTSD). The paper reports whole-brain, voxel-wise between-group contrasts with peak Talairach coordinates and T-scores for regions showing reduced GM in PTSD (bilateral insula, left medial frontal gyrus), satisfying availability of coordinate tables/figures. Both groups are adults (mean ages ~33). Controls are trauma-exposed non-PTSD individuals (acceptable). Full text includes background, methods (VBM, fMRI), results (coordinates), and discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7 are met; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, peer-reviewed English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to compare grey matter volume between recent-onset PTSD patients and control groups. The paper reports whole-brain, voxel-wise between-group contrasts (PTSD vs controls and non-PTSD vs controls) with family-wise error correction and cluster extent thresholds, and presents regional results (figures/tables) consistent with whole-brain analyses. Control groups include both trauma-exposed non-PTSD survivors and non-trauma-exposed healthy controls. Participants are adult male miners (adult sample). The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria are met (e.g., not ROI-only, not pediatric, reports significant between-group whole-brain results).

This is an empirical, peer-reviewed adult human MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to compare gray matter density between combat-exposed PTSD patients and controls (combat-exposed without PTSD and their unexposed cotwins). The full text includes background, methods (VBM whole-brain analyses with smoothing, SPM, small-volume corrections), results (voxel-wise between-group contrasts with peak coordinates, tables, and figures), and discussion. It reports whole-brain voxel-wise PTSD vs control contrasts and significant loci (hippocampus, pregenual ACC, insula) with coordinates and small-volume-corrected p-values. Controls are trauma-exposed and unexposed veterans (acceptable). Sample comprises adult Vietnam veterans. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, I7 and violates no exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical, adult, English MRI study comparing PTSD patients to healthy controls and reports global gray matter volumetric differences and hippocampal ROI volumes, but it does NOT report any whole-brain voxel-wise between-group contrast (e.g., VBM) of gray-matter volume. Exclusion criteria met: E4 (only ROI analyses / no qualifying whole‑brain results) and E7 (morphometry performed by non‑voxel‑based methods only: manual hippocampal tracing and global SIENAX volumes rather than voxel‑wise GM contrasts). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (empirical MRI study assessing GM volume differences), I6 (healthy control population), I7 (adult sample). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (no whole‑brain voxel-wise between-group GM contrast reported). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore excluded because the paper lacks the required whole‑brain voxel-wise GM contrast required by the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, English-language adult MRI study that reports manual ROI volumetry (amygdala/hippocampus) comparing trauma-exposed adults with and without PTSD and also reports voxel-based morphometry (VBM) processing/correlational analyses. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (empirical MRI GM volume comparison), I5 (results reported in main text/figures), I6 (trauma-exposed controls without PTSD acceptable), I7 (adult sample). However, the paper does NOT report a whole-brain voxel-wise between-group (PTSD vs controls) VBM contrast of grey-matter volume; the VBM work reported are correlational voxel-wise analyses and covariate/interactions rather than a direct whole-brain PTSD vs control GM contrast. Therefore it fails I4 and meets exclusion E4 (ROI analyses with no qualifying whole-brain between-group results). Full text appears complete. Conclusion: EXCLUDE for meta-analysis because no qualifying whole-brain PTSD vs control voxel-wise GM contrast was reported.

This is an empirical MRI study using voxel-based morphometry and SPM reporting whole-brain voxel-wise GM volume contrasts between PTSD and controls (I3, I4). Results (coordinates/figures) are presented (I5). Controls are healthy matched individuals (I6). However, the sample is pediatric (subjects ages 7–14; explicitly described as children/adolescents), so it fails the adult sample requirement (I7) and thus meets exclusion criterion E6 (pediatric study). Therefore the study must be excluded from this meta-analysis focused on adult PTSD morphometry.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study of adults with acute PTSD (ages 18–65) versus matched healthy controls that reports whole-brain voxel-based morphometry (VBM) between-group contrasts with coordinates and corrected p-values, assessing gray-matter differences. Volumetric analyses are also reported. The full text (background, methods, results, discussion) is available. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, I6, and I7. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, non-voxel methods only, pediatric sample) apply.

Although this is an empirical, adult MRI study of trauma-exposed victims with and without PTSD, the paper does not report a whole-brain voxel-wise between-group contrast of GM volume comparing PTSD patients vs controls. The MRI analyses reported are within-group voxel-based correlations (P300 amplitude vs GM density) in the PTSD group (N=6 with MRI) and reference prior between-group findings in a separate publication. Therefore it fails the required inclusion criteria I3 (study-level between-group GM volume comparison) and I4 (whole-brain voxel-wise between-group contrast). It meets inclusion criteria I6 (trauma-exposed control group) and I7 (adult sample). It thus should be excluded under E10 (reports only within-group results without a qualifying between-group contrast). Full text appears complete.

This is a treatment (CBT) study that uses voxel-based morphometry and reports pretreatment rACC volume correlations with treatment outcome and contrasts between PTSD subgroups (responders vs nonresponders) and control groups. However, it does not report a whole-brain voxel-wise between-group contrast of PTSD patients (as a combined group) versus controls. Therefore it fails the required inclusion criterion I4 and meets exclusion criterion E9 (treatment study without a qualifying PTSD vs control whole-brain contrast). Satisfied inclusion criteria: I3 (empirical English MRI study assessing GM volume), I5 (reports coordinates/figures for voxel-wise results), I6 (uses trauma-exposed and healthy controls), I7 (adult human sample). Not met: I4 (no whole-brain voxel-wise PTSD vs control contrast). Consequently, exclude from the meta-analysis.

Exclusion ID met: E6 (paediatric/adolescent sample). Inclusion IDs met: I3 (empirical MRI study assessing GM volume differences), I4 (reports whole-brain voxel-wise VBM between-group contrasts), I5 (results presented in figures/tables), I6 (control population is trauma-exposed non-PTSD). Inclusion ID not met: I7 (sample restricted to adults) — this study’s sample is adolescents (mean age 15.15 years, range 8–19), so does not meet the adult-sample requirement. Full text appears complete. Therefore the study must be excluded from this adult PTSD morphometry meta-analysis.

This is an empirical, English-language structural MRI study using voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to compare gray matter between PTSD patients and controls (fire survivors). It reports whole-brain voxel-wise between-group contrasts with Talairach coordinates, SPM maps, and a table of significant loci (left hippocampus, left ACC, bilateral insula). Controls are trauma-exposed individuals without PTSD; sample are adults (mean ages ~34). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and therefore appears complete. All required inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, English-language MRI study of adults that used voxel-based morphometry (VBM) to perform whole-brain, voxel-wise between-group contrasts comparing recent-onset PTSD patients to trauma-exposed non-PTSD controls. The paper reports significant GM volume decreases (coordinates and figures/tables provided) in left hippocampus and bilateral calcarine cortex, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain voxel-wise results. Both groups are adult miners (mean ages >18). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not pediatric, not non-empirical, includes a qualifying between-group contrast with positive findings). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete.
